label: Input-phase step t>=2 through <DEL> (encoding phase, off during copy)
explanation: Fires on almost every original-input step from t=2 onward and on the <DEL> step, and is essentially silent at t=0,1 and throughout the copy phase (333 copy-phase activations out of 2.5M, about 0% of mass). Token identity, L, digits and first token barely matter. Magnitude: the <DEL> step is the strongest (93% firing rate, about 28% of mass, higher mean per active step than original steps), and the top examples ramp up within the sequence toward <DEL>. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire much less often (rate 0.09 vs 0.66). Firing rate falls off at late original positions in long sequences (t=8,9). The false positives are mostly those repeated-token steps and weak late steps.

issues: The predicate and label hold up. Test split: P 0.928, R 1.000, F1 0.963, mass recall 1.000. The test misses are 282 steps holding 0.0% of the mass, and they are scattered weak copy-phase steps. The false positives look scattered: firing rate is about 0.87-0.97 across orig_idx 2-8 and flat across in_tok, first_tok, n_digits and L. No systematic class turned up.

The in_first claim in the explanation is false; it is a confound with the copy phase. The 0.09 vs 0.66 rate comes from in_first=0 being mostly copy-phase steps. Within the input phase, repeated tokens fire just as often as first occurrences. Dev split precision: (t>=2)&(phase==0)&(in_first==0) = 0.934 and (t>=2)&(phase==0)&(in_first==1) = 0.925. So 'repeated-token steps fire much less often' and 'most false positives are these repeated-token steps' are both wrong.

The claim that the rate drops at late original positions (t=8,9) is also a confound. The by-t rates (0.35 at t=8, 0.17 at t=9) mix in copy-phase steps from shorter sequences. By orig_idx the rate is 0.93 at index 7 and 0.85 at index 8, and (phase==0)&(orig_idx>=7) has precision 0.903. That is at most a mild drop, not a strong one.

These claims check out: silent at t=0,1 (0 active); copy phase has 333 active steps and ~0% of mass; <DEL> fires 93.4% of the time with 28% of the mass on ~18% of active steps, so it has the highest mean; little dependence on token, L, digit count or first token.
